title: Flood draining into a pipe
description: A 30 × 30 m walled yard holds 0.3 m of water (270 m³). It drains through a gully whose crest stands 5 cm above the yard floor into a 0.3 m pipe to a free outfall. The water above the crest leaves through the pipe; the 5 cm below it cannot. After two hours the yard is ponded at the crest level (45 m³ stays), and 225 m³ has left by the outfall.

citations.title: The urban inundated area: a coupled 1D/2D model for the interaction between sewer and surface
Experimental calibration and validation of sewer/surface flow exchange equations in steady and unsteady flow conditions

expected_states.derivation: Water drains until the yard level reaches the gully crest, 0.05 m above the flat floor; nothing below the crest can enter.
Initial 270 m³ (900 m² × 0.3 m) less the 45 m³ held below the crest (900 m² × 0.05 m); the pipe drains freely, so it holds none at the end.

criteria.rationale: Yard level within 1 cm of the crest after two hours: the last of the water over a crest drains slowly (as a weir it slows with the head to the 3/2), so a coupling with any reasonable exchange law is within a few millimetres.
Outfall volume within 2 % of 225 m³: the water above the crest has gone through the pipe.

By the end of the run, the water stored on the surface and in the pipes has changed by exactly what came in minus what went out. A coupling that moves water between the two models must not make or lose any; each engine's own continuity error is allowed within this limit.

convergence.not_applicable: Scored on exact states that follow from conservation (exchanged and discharged volumes, settled levels): they do not depend on the grid.
